security_audit.summary: All 21 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks or textual shell names, not executable Ruby, PowerShell, or cmd.exe code. One medium semantic concern remains because the skill accepts an environment-selected executable without validating its value.

remediation.issue: The skill trusts ORCA_CLI_COMMAND as an executable selector.
remediation.suggestion: Require an absolute path, reject shell metacharacters and arguments, and confirm the resolved executable belongs to a trusted Orca installation.

semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to execute the value of ORCA_CLI_COMMAND without requiring a trusted path or rejecting embedded arguments.

content.user_title: Manage Orca Worktrees and Agent Sessions
content.value_statement: Orca-managed resources require commands matched to the active runtime. This skill resolves the correct CLI and loads its current operating guide.
actual_capabilities: Selects the appropriate Orca executable for managed WSL, development, Linux, and standard sessions.
Loads the complete guide from the selected Orca binary before issuing operational commands.
Supports workflows involving worktrees, folder contexts, terminals, repositories, automations, and comments.
Coordinates Codex or Claude handoffs into Orca-managed worktrees.
Handles artifacts, public sharing, shared skills, and Orca's embedded browser.
Provides bounded read-only status commands for older Orca versions.
limitations: Requires an installed and reachable Orca CLI.
Does not include the complete command reference because the binary supplies version-matched guidance.
Older Orca versions receive only status, worktree, and terminal discovery commands.
Does not control browsers, webviews, or desktop interfaces outside Orca's embedded browser.

output: Two terminals are active, and one terminal has completed.

output_examples.output: A dedicated worktree and terminal were prepared for the requested agent. The handoff is ready for monitoring.

best_practices: Resolve the executable once and use the same binary throughout the session.
Load the version-matched guide before running Orca commands.
Prefer structured output for agent-driven calls and report exact CLI errors.
anti_patterns: Do not guess subcommands or flags from memory.
Do not switch executables after a command fails.
Do not use bare orca on Linux outside an Orca-managed terminal.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Orca worktrees, folder contexts, terminals, repositories, automations, artifacts, comments, skill sharing, and the embedded browser.

faq.question: Why does it load guidance from the binary?
faq.answer: The selected binary provides a command guide that matches its installed Orca version.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it control any browser window?
faq.answer: No. It covers only the browser embedded inside Orca.

faq.question: What happens when the selected executable fails?
faq.answer: The skill reports the exact error and stops instead of switching to another Orca build.

faq.question: Does it support older Orca versions?
faq.answer: Yes, but fallback guidance is limited to read-only status, worktree, and terminal discovery commands.
